comparison: Both evaluate the primary CSD locus mapping as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on genetic mapping, LOH patterns, and statistical significance (C7, C43-C48). Peer review accepts the same core claims (C7, C44-C48) plus mechanism claims (C49-C50), describing the analyses as 'solid, well-executed' with 'convincing support.'

OpenEval R2 addresses mechanistic evidence for crossover recombination (C49-C50, C86, C104) as SUPPORTED. Peer R1 includes C49-C50 in their acceptance of the mapping methodology. Both agree on the copy-neutral LOH mechanism.

Perfect claim overlap (C8, C60, C73, C75). Both evaluate elevated genetic diversity and balancing selection as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes limited sample size; peer review accepts this as part of 'solid genomic analyses' supporting ancient origin.

Perfect claim overlap (C9-C10, C61). Both evaluate the non-coding nature of sex determination as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes lack of functional validation; peer review explicitly affirms 'convincing support for the ancient origin of a non-coding locus.'

High overlap on homology claims (C11-C12, C54-C56). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with caveat about functional conservation. Peer R4 also includes C57 and accepts comparative genomic analysis supporting ancient conservation without challenge.

Perfect claim overlap (C13, C76). Both evaluate ancient conservation inference as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes need for functional validation; peer review explicitly affirms 'convincing support for the ancient origin' and 'valuable insights into evolutionary conservation.'

Perfect claim overlap (C51-C52, C81). Both evaluate the anomalous heterozygous diploid males as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval explicitly states the finding is unresolved; peer review implicitly acknowledges this through noting lack of novel advances and functional validation.

High overlap (C65-C66, C78). Both evaluate clonal line differences in diploid male production as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance; peer review accepts as part of 'solid, well-executed' genomic analyses. Peer R7 also includes C58 on universality.

Partial overlap on C58. OpenEval evaluates universality of CSD locus across clonal lines as SUPPORTED. Peer R7 groups this with clonal line difference claims (C65-C66, C78), accepting all as part of solid genomic analyses.

Perfect claim overlap (C62-C64). Both evaluate differential expression analysis as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes small sample size and timing limitations; peer review accepts this as part of authors' considerable efforts to conduct functional analyses within data limits.

High overlap (C70-C71). Both evaluate tra heterozygosity and sex-specific splicing as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes tra's downstream role; peer review accepts as part of solid genomic analyses. Peer R9 also includes C77 on lack of honeybee-like mechanism.

Partial overlap on C77. OpenEval evaluates lack of tra locus homology as SUPPORTED, distinguishing from honeybee mechanism. Peer R9 groups this with tra characterization (C70-C71), accepting the distinction without challenge.

High overlap (C67, C79-C80). Both evaluate negative findings from QTL1 analysis as SUPPORTED. OpenEval argues against second CSD locus; peer review accepts genome-wide mapping as thorough. Peer R10 also includes evolutionary claims C68-C69.

Partial overlap (C68-C69). OpenEval evaluates evolutionary relationship discussion as SUPPORTED with speculation noted. Peer R10 groups these with QTL1 analysis (C67, C79-C80), accepting comparative genomic work without challenge.

Minimal overlap on C10 (non-coding nature). OpenEval R4 evaluates protein-coding gene analysis as SUPPORTED. Peer R11 addresses mechanistic speculation (C93) as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of functional validation and novel advances.

Partial overlap on C93. OpenEval evaluates transvection speculation as SUPPORTED but explicitly speculative. Peer R11 evaluates as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of functional validation and that the study 'does not offer novel conceptual or experimental advances.'

Minimal overlap on C57. OpenEval evaluates unannotated lncRNA finding as SUPPORTED but lacking functional characterization. Peer R4 groups this with homology claims (C11-C12, C54-C56), accepting as part of comparative genomic analysis.
